summary: An irregular line segment connected to the terminal of a vertical/horizontal bar perpendicular to grid edge wraps around a nearby obstacle sprite and repositions while preserving total pixel count.
src: irregular line segment attached to terminal of edge-perpendicular bar s
dst: wrap around nearest obstacle sprite d
path: connect s.bar_terminal to d.nearest_pixel, traverse d.boundary pixels, exit at d.farthest_corner with 45-degree diagonal extension
trajectory: paint s.color along path; total painted pixels == len(s.original_segment)
transform: s.original_segment -> disappear; repaint along new wrapped path
multi_step: Step 1: identify bar perpendicular to grid edge and its attached irregular segment s; Step 2: identify obstacle sprite d nearest to bar terminal; Step 3: compute shortest path from bar terminal to d; Step 4: traverse d boundary clockwise/counterclockwise; Step 5: exit at far corner with 45-degree diagonal; Step 6: repaint s pixels along new path preserving count
notes: Key insight: the irregular segment 'swings' around the obstacle like a rope, connecting to nearest point, hugging the obstacle boundary, then exiting diagonally. Total segment length (pixel count) is conserved.
